program: Birth and postpartum support, doula development and perinatal advocacy

what: Chicago Volunteer Doulas connects families with pregnancy, birth, postpartum and pregnancy-loss support.
Its doulas provide practical, emotional and advocacy support, including for families facing barriers to care.
The organization also supports doula training, compensation and community partnerships.
strengths: Continuous labor support has a plausible evidence-backed route to better birth experiences.
Local access and postpartum help may reduce burdens on under-resourced families.
Training and compensation can strengthen the available doula workforce.
reservations: Local unique births and incremental outcomes were not verified.
Older low-certainty trials do not establish local mortality or long-term infant effects.
Coverage alternatives, household costs, provider opportunity costs and finances require further diligence.

sections.what: Chicago Volunteer Doulas Inc, EIN 27-3636022, supports labor, postpartum and pregnancy-loss care and doula workforce development. Official sources identify Chicago South and West Side beneficiaries despite a Springfield mailing address. The current giving page supports fair compensation, training and under-resourced family care. Services are not uniformly free: the current matching page describes a $25 nonrefundable contribution for traditional labor support, paid professionals and postpartum support options. No donation transaction was tested.
sections.monitoring: The current impact introduction covers October 1, 2025 through September 1, 2026, an eleven-month service period, not a verified annual unique birth cohort. Its full linked report was inaccessible in this bounded check. Observe completed distinct local births and postpartum care, coverage alternatives, actual delivery mode, adverse events, family time and out-of-pocket costs, doula payment after opportunity costs and collected reimbursements. Training targets do not establish new doulas' net earnings or incremental births served.
sections.qualitative: Cochrane's 2017 review, searched mainly through October 2016, pools 26 usable trials and finds possible reductions in cesarean birth and negative birth experiences. Evidence quality is low and settings differ. The .75 pooled cesarean risk ratio is an external observation; applying it locally requires explicit transport and coverage judgments. No apparent special-care nursery or breastfeeding benefit was established. Low Apgar scores are not infant lifetime QALYs or deaths prevented. This reference gives no maternal or infant mortality credit and no additional ordinary survivor wages. Infant health is unknown-neutral centrally, with signed acute stresses rather than a factual zero claim.
sections.cost:
FY2024 original recognized annual cost is $708,622. Direct event and reviewed rental fields are zero; no netted addback was identified. FY2023 cost is $493,603 and FY2022 $479,599, giving a comparable October–September annual mean of $560,608. Donated-service fields are zero in the latest two returns; this does not establish zero unpaid social cost. The whole recipient denominator includes training and nonclinical work while the numerator prices a limited conditional birth-support channel, not a verified marginal expansion.

A judged 300 local birth-household opportunities and .5 additional annual-work response give 150 exposed households; .8 delivery uptake gives 120 supported births. A judged .32 cesarean baseline, external .75 risk ratio and .5 local transport attenuation imply 4.8 avoided cesareans. A .02 integrated acute physical-recovery QALY per avoided cesarean and .002 integrated emotional birth-experience QALY per supported birth are judgments, truncated within the first postpartum year, not permanent utilities. The experience area explicitly excludes physical surgical recovery and is not a depression effect; an additional conservative overlap adjustment guards residual shared welfare. Retaining .8 of positive components for overlap and discounting a quarter-year delay at 3% gives .266821 clinical QALYs. Negative clinical components remain full. Maternal and infant health are distinct persons; no mortality, Apgar conversion or infant lifelong outcome is added.

Resource exposure does not depend on clinical effect. Forty-five parent households have a judged $200 net care/work-resource gain, retain .5 for health overlap, then incur the full $50 burden: $50 net. The other 105 lose $50. The $50 includes the observed $25 traditional-support contribution plus a judged $25 travel, care or time burden; applying this uniformly is a conditional service-mix assumption, not a statement that every family pays it. Gains are after taxes, benefits, replacement earnings and new costs; no retail doula fee is counted as income.

Ten distinct provider households incur a judged $200 net unpaid-time/foregone-resource burden at a $40,000 baseline. Net provider compensation is unknown-neutral centrally, not observed zero; a $1,000 net-gain sensitivity excludes taxes and alternative earnings. Parent baseline is $30,000, one welfareperson per household and one finite year. Joint household resources before a single log give −.074614 equivalents including providers; combined .192207 yields $36.867559 million per ten combined equivalents. This signed ledger is not ten clinical QALYs.

Clinical parent households are a subset of all parent resource exposure. Provider households are assumed disjoint, giving a 160-household union for general harm stress; their time burdens remain even when birth benefits fail. Positive overlap never shrinks negative resources or unavoidable costs. Matched local payer and external care cost stresses are explicit. Central counterparty neutrality is unknown, not complete-world benefit; public and insurer opportunity costs, nonlocal incidence and the full portfolio remain unpriced.
sections.funding: Illinois Medicaid coverage for certified enrolled doulas is an existing alternative, effective February 2024 under the December 2024 notice, not a new donation's entire benefit. CVD's training toward reimbursement eligibility supplies a mechanism but does not establish collected additional income or net new service. Original FY2024 government grants are zero; net assets are −$59,881. Negative reported assets and liabilities warrant accounting and liquidity diligence, not a conclusion that services have stopped. The cost return predates the new impact period. No priced unfunded expansion or donor replacement rate was verified. The .5 response prior represents additional annual funded work against existing coverage and providers; b=1 is exposed separately.

model.geographicAttribution: Chicago birth households and assumed local distinct provider households; postal location not beneficiary attribution.
model.formula: births=N*b*uptake; avoided cesareans=births*baselineRisk*(1−externalRR)*transport. Q=positiveOnly(avoided*acuteQ,k)+positiveOnly(births*experienceQ,k)+positiveOnly(births*infantQ,k)−full union harm, discounted once. Household net precedes .5*people*log(1+net/baseline). Price=10*C/(clinical+resources).
model.counterfactual: Covered Medicaid doulas, family companions, paid providers and alternative community programs continue.
model.attribution: Local cohort, annual response, delivery, transport, utility and resource changes are conditional judgments; external risk ratio is not a local causal observation.
model.uncertainty: Complete portfolio, local birth and infant outcomes, net compensation, payer incidence and marginal funding unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Completed supported births, finite avoided cesarean and birth-experience burdens, signed parent care/work resources and provider opportunity costs; no mortality credit.
